problem: A plate of mass $M$ occupies region bounded by two circles ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1$ and ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4.$ Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3}{14\pi }M\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis.

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Radius of Gyration of a Plane Lamina

feedback.problem: A plate of mass $M$ occupies the part of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 2$ for $x\ge 0.$ Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{2M}{\pi }{y}^{2}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{2},\,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{2M}{\pi }{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2M}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{r}^{5}{sin}^{4}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2M}{\pi }({\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{sin}^{4}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2M}{\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{6}{r}^{6}{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\cdot ({\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{(\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2M}{\pi }\cdot \frac{4}{3}\cdot ({\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\frac{1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡2\theta }{4}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{8M}{3\pi }\cdot ({\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{4}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{2}+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡2\theta }{4}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{8M}{3\pi }\cdot ({\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{4}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta +1}{8}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{8M}{3\pi }\cdot ({\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\frac{3}{8}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta }{8}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{8M}{3\pi }\cdot {[\frac{3\theta }{8}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }{4}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡4\theta }{32}]}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{8M}{3\pi }\cdot \frac{3\pi }{8} \\  & =M.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{M\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
